title: Teddy Willow and the Humming Log
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a forest so green and dappled with sunshine, lived a very special teddy bear named Teddy Willow. Teddy Willow was not just any teddy bear. He was a teddy bear who knew how to listen. His button eyes, sewn on with careful stitches, were always wide open, watching the world with quiet curiosity. He’d watch the ladybirds tiptoe across fuzzy leaves and the busy ants march in straight lines.

Every day Teddy Willow would find his favourite spot by the sturdy old oak tree. He’d sit there, his soft brown fur warmed by the gentle sunbeams that peeked through the branches. From his cosy spot he’d listen to the forest’s happy sounds: the swish-swish of the leaves, the happy chirps of tiny birds, and the gentle sigh of the breeze. Teddy Willow loved the quiet wonders of his forest home, though sometimes he just listened, and did not always join in the fun.

Until one day something new tickled Teddy Willow’s fuzzy ears. It was not the usual chirp or rustle. It was a sound so soft and sweet, like a sleepy song sung just for him, a lullaby drifting on the air. This lovely humming sound was coming from a big fallen hollow log nestled at the edge of the meadow. The log seemed to sing, a melody as sweet and soothing as his Mama’s bedtime songs. Teddy Willow tilted his head, his button eyes growing even wider. He wondered, with his button eyes wide, what made the log sing such a happy tune.

Teddy Willow knew he simply had to discover the secret of the humming log. He carefully stood up, his stuffing settling comfortably. He looked around for his very best friend, Pecan the chipmunk. Pecan was usually a whirlwind of activity, busy burying tasty nuts or scampering up the tallest trees, his bushy tail twitching like a happy flag. “Pecan,” Teddy Willow called out, his voice as soft as a whispered secret.

Pecan’s little head popped out from behind a patch of plump green clover, his nose twitching and his whiskers wiggling. “Hello there, Teddy Willow. What’s all the happy fuss about?” Pecan, always in a hurry, darted a little closer. He almost tumbled over a large brown leaf, thinking it was a very sleepy nut.

“I heard a humming,” Teddy Willow explained, his voice full of gentle curiosity. “A lovely soft lullaby, coming from the hollow log over there. Have you heard it, Pecan?”

Pecan’s bright beady eyes sparkled like tiny shiny marbles. “A humming log, you say? Oh, Teddy Willow, that sounds like a grand adventure waiting to happen. Let’s go investigate this musical log right away.” And with a happy chitter, Pecan dashed ahead, Teddy Willow following at his own steady pace. They made their way towards the mysterious hollow log.

Because of that, Teddy Willow and Pecan approached the big fallen log very, very quietly. They tiptoed as softly as dandelion fluff floating on the breeze. As they got closer and closer, the humming sound grew a little louder, a gentle vibration that tickled their paws and made their whiskers buzz ever so slightly. The entrance to the log smelled wonderfully of damp earth, sweet velvety moss, and something else, something a little bit exciting and new. It was a smell that felt safe and cosy.

Until finally they stepped inside. The air grew warm and smelled of sweet earth and velvet moss. A soft steady humming filled their ears, and a gentle twinkling light danced before their eyes. To Teddy Willow’s surprise, it was not dark and spooky at all. The inside of the log was actually quite bright. Little pinpricks of light, like tiny stars fallen to earth, twinkled all around them, clinging to the inside walls. As their eyes slowly adjusted to the soft glow, they saw them: the source of the humming and the light. Tiny shimmering glow-worms, no bigger than a little ladybird, glowing with the most beautiful steady light. And as they glowed, they made the humming sound, a gentle happy hum. It was like a secret tiny orchestra of light and music, just for them.

Teddy Willow and Pecan understood the wonderful secret of the humming log. The glow-worms were not just making light to see by. They were making a song, a happy song with their humming, a song of making the world a little bit brighter and sharing warmth with each other. Teddy Willow felt a lovely warm feeling spread all the way from his button nose to his stuffing toes. Pecan sat very still beside him, his twitchy nose finally calm for a moment, completely captivated by the beautiful gentle music. They stayed there for a long happy time, just listening to the song and watching the pretty lights dance.

Ever since then, whenever Teddy Willow and Pecan felt a little quiet inside, or when the forest seemed extra sleepy and peaceful, they knew just what to do. They would visit the humming log. They’d sit just outside its entrance, listening to the glow-worms’ gentle happy song, the same song that had first tickled Teddy Willow’s fuzzy ears by the oak, and they would yawn, and the log would hum them toward rest, as logs and lullabies will.
